officials.name: Jeff Fletcher
officials.address: 102 E. Wall Street, Harrisonville, Missouri 64701
officials.bio: Jeff Fletcher began his service as Cass County’s North Commissioner for District 2 on January 1, 2025. Prior to this role, Jeff served as the Cass County Clerk for six years, where he and his staff ensured accurate and efficient elections, working tirelessly to protect the voting rights of all Cass County residents. Jeff takes great pride in his work for Cass County and looks forward to continuing his dedication to constituents as North Commissioner.

officials.name: Larry Vincent
officials.bio: Larry Vincent was appointed to the office of Cole County Collector of Revenue on October 3, 2007, by Governor Matt Blunt. Mr. Vincent is a 5-time past elected councilman for the City of Jefferson, and has a background in the insurance/brokerage field as president and general manager of the property and casualty division for a local agency. He has served on many community boards and has a strong commitment to serving the citizens of Cole County.

officials.name: Harry Otto
officials.address: 311 E High Street Jefferson City, MO 65101
officials.bio: Born and raised in Osage County, Harry Otto graduated from the University of Mo-Columbia with a B.S. in Business Administration. He has a career as a CPA, served in the US Army Reserve, and held several MO state government positions. He is active in the Cole County community and is honored to serve as the Western District Commissioner.

officials.name: Jeff Hoelscher
officials.bio: Jeff Hoelscher is a graduate of Blair Oaks High School and Lincoln University with a BS in Agricultural Business. He owns Hoelscher Enterprises, LLC, a construction and remodeling business, and holds a Broker-Salesperson Realty License. He also volunteers as a youth sports coach.

officials.name: Sam Bushman
officials.bio: Sam Bushman was born and raised in Cole County, attending Jefferson City Public Schools, Lincoln University, and the University of Missouri. He was a businessman in Downtown Jefferson City for over 40 years, selling his business in 2022. Sam has served as Presiding Commissioner of Cole County since 2014 and holds various board positions.

officials.name: Bob Tullock
officials.bio: Bob Tullock was first elected to represent the residents of District 7 in 2023. He is a Conservative Republican who believes that elected officials are there to serve as your elected representative. Bob is a retired business owner and a licensed pilot.

officials.name: Brian Haskins
officials.bio: Brian Haskins, a 1974 graduate of Northwest R-1, was elected to a four-year term to the Jefferson County Council in November 2018. He has served on the Northwest R-1 School Board and High Ridge Fire Protection District, and is currently President of the Jefferson County Parks Foundation. Mr. Haskins owns and operates a family business in High Ridge, where he resides with his wife Becky, with whom he has 4 children and 13 grandchildren.

officials.name: Charles Groeteke
officials.bio: Charles is the senior member of the Council, serving in his fourth term on your County Council. He returned to office in January of 2017, marking his 12th year of service to the citizens of District 4 by 2026. He resides in Barnhart with his wife, Sharon.

officials.name: Lori Arons
officials.bio: Lori Arons was appointed to fill the vacancy in District #3 on January 29th, 2024, when Shannon Otto resigned. She has been a resident of Jefferson County since 2001 and retired from teaching in 2020 after over 30 years. Prior to her appointment, Lori was actively involved with county government and founded a non-partisan Facebook group focused on responsible development.

officials.name: Abe McGull
officials.bio: Abram “Abe” McGull was elected to City Council to represent Zone 2 in April 2019 and re-elected in April 2023. Councilmember McGull currently serves as the Chair of the City Council Plans and Policies Committee and as a member of the City Council Public Involvement Committee. He was honorably discharged from the United States Navy in 2012 with the rank of Commander and received the Bronze Star for his outstanding performance in Iraq.

officials.name: Brandon Jenson
officials.bio: Brandon Jenson was elected to the Zone 3 Council Seat in April 2023 and serves as Chair of the City Council Finance and Administration Committee. He holds bachelor's degrees from Missouri State University and currently serves as the Director of Community Impact at United Way of the Ozarks. His term will expire in April 2027.

officials.name: Bruce Adib-Yazdi
officials.bio: Bruce Adib-Yazdi was elected to the Zone 4 Council Seat in April 2025. He currently serves on the City Council Finance and Administration Committee, the City Council Public Involvement Committee, and as the City Council Liaison to the Ozarks Headwaters Recycling and Materials Management District.

officials.name: Callie Carroll
officials.bio: Callie Carroll was elected to City Council to serve as General Seat C in April 2023. She holds a bachelor's and master's degree from Missouri State University and has a background in broadcast journalism and athletics development. Currently, she is the Business Development and Shareholder Relations Officer at Old Missouri Bank and serves on several boards and committees.

officials.name: Craig Hosmer
officials.bio: Craig Hosmer was elected to City Council to serve as General Council Seat B in April 2013 and re-elected in April 2017, April 2021, and April 2025. Councilmember Hosmer currently serves as a member of the City Council Finance and Administration Committee and the City Council Plans and Policies Committee. Councilmember Hosmer also serves as the City Council Liaison to the Mayor’s Commission for Children.

officials.name: Derek Lee
officials.bio: Derek Lee was elected to City Council to represent General Council Seat D in April 2023. He serves as Chair of the City Council Public Involvement Committee and as a member of the City Council Community Involvement Committee, and is the City Council Liaison to the Ozarks Transportation Organization. He holds a master’s degree in civil engineering and has owned and operated Lee Engineering and Associates in Springfield for 23 years.

officials.name: Heather Hardinger
officials.bio: Heather Hardinger was elected to City Council to represent General Council Seat A in April 2021 and re-elected in April 2025. Mayor Pro Tem Hardinger currently serves on several City Council committees and as the City Council Liaison to the Springfield Sister Cities Association. She is a chief diversity officer for CoxHealth and holds a master's in political science.

officials.name: Monica Horton
officials.bio: Monica Horton is a member of Springfield City Council, appointed in 2022 and re-elected to serve a 4-year term until April 2029. As the Zone 1 Councilmember, she focuses on policymaking and budget advocacy to address issues like chronic nuisance properties, housing, park improvements, and systemic poverty, aiming for livability and economic mobility in Zone 1. She also serves on the Finance and Administration Committee, the Community Involvement Committee, and the City Council American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Review Committee.

officials.name: Jeff Schrag
officials.address: Busch Municipal Building 840 Boonville Avenue Springfield, MO 65802
officials.bio: Jeff Schrag was elected Mayor of Springfield, Missouri, in April 2025. Schrag is a seasoned small business owner and community leader. His entrepreneurial spirit has led him to establish and acquire multiple businesses across diverse industries, providing him with firsthand experience in the complexities of navigating local economies and the impact of government policies.

officials.name: Derrick Thomas
officials.office: Chair/Organization dedicated to residential home development and construction
officials.address: 1520 Market Street, Suite 2080 Saint Louis, Missouri 63103
officials.bio: Commissioner Thomas has experience in real estate development (custom homes, town homes, and condos), general contracting, property management, architectural design, and real estate consulting. He currently serves on the Home Builders Association board of trustees and steering committee of 50+ housing Council.

officials.name: John Wuest
officials.address: 1520 Market Street, Suite 2080 Saint Louis, Missouri 63103
officials.bio: Commissioner Wuest has served as President and CEO of the St. Louis Equity Fund from 2005 through 2015, and as Vice Chair from 2016 through 2017. Prior to joining the Equity Fund, he served as President and CEO of Heartland Bank and Executive Vice President and COO of Love Development and Real Estate Company. He began his banking career with Mercantile Bank (now U.S. Bank) rising to Executive Vice President-Commercial Lending.

officials.name: Marc Hirshman
officials.address: 1520 Market Street, Suite 2080 Saint Louis, Missouri 63103
officials.bio: Commissioner Hirshman received his Bachelor of Arts degree in economics and finance from the University of Illinois and both his J.D. and LL.M. in Taxation with academic honors from Chicago-Kent College of Law. He is Co-Founder and President of Twain Financial Partners, an investment management firm located in St. Louis, MO with over $4B in assets under management within the public-private partnership sector.

officials.name: Deanetta James
officials.address: 1520 Market Street, Suite 2080 Saint Louis, Missouri 63103
officials.bio: Commissioner James has experience working with low/moderated income families. She has served as President of Community Renewal and Development, Inc., and on several Boards, including Macler Shepard Senior Apartment Association, Urban League of Metropolitan St. Louis.

officials.name: Gail Brown
officials.address: 1520 Market Street, Suite 2080 Saint Louis, Missouri 63103
officials.bio: Gail Brown holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Economics and Business and a Masters Degree in Business Administration. She is the president of Brown-Kortkamp Realty and Urban Planning and Development Corporation (UPDC), and serves as an appointed commissioner for the St. Louis City Affordable Housing Commission and Tax Increment Financing Commission.

officials.bio: Commissioner Jones is the Vice President and Missouri State Director of SEIU Healthcare IL/IN/MO/KS; the union represents over 70,000 healthcare and childcare providers in four states.

officials.name: Paula Foster
officials.office: Commissioner/Tenant in Subsidized or Rent Assisted Housing
officials.address: 1520 Market Street, Suite 2080 Saint Louis, Missouri 63103
officials.bio: The ordinance that created the Commission requires that one member living in subsidized housing be appointed to represent tenant interests. As a public housing resident, and as President of the Blumeyer Association, Commissioner foster brings to the Commission problem solving and organizational procedures experience.

officials.name: April Ford Griffin
officials.address: 1520 Market Street, Suite 2080 Saint Louis, Missouri 63103
officials.bio: April Ford Griffin has forged a distinguished professional career focused on improving the lives of children, families, senior citizens, and addressing blighted neighborhoods. Appointed Executive Director of the Affordable Housing Commission (AHC) in 2013, she supervises the implementation of loan, grant, and other AHC-approved programs, coordinating efforts with city and private agencies.
